title: HTTP security headers checklist
when: A server or static host sends replies and the standard protective HTTP headers must be set correctly for pages, APIs and downloads.
inputs: whether the site is HTTPS only
prompt:
Goal: One function sets a reviewed header set on every reply, tuned per reply kind, and a test checks it on the running server.
Steps:
1. Pages: Content-Security-Policy (its own playbook), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() unless used.
2. Framing: frame-ancestors 'none' in the policy plus X-Frame-Options: DENY for old browsers.
3. HTTPS only sites: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, only after every subdomain serves HTTPS; never on localhost.
4. Isolation: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin for private assets.
5. APIs: Content-Type with charset on JSON, Cache-Control: no-store on personal data, no X-Powered-By and no detailed Server header.
6. User file downloads: Content-Disposition: attachment with an encoded safe filename, plus nosniff.
Quality bar:
- Error replies and 404s carry the headers too.
- Each header has a one line reason next to it.
- A test fetches a page, an API route and a 404 and asserts the set.
Pitfalls:
- HSTS includeSubDomains before every subdomain is ready, locking users out.
- X-XSS-Protection: 1, which is obsolete; send 0 or omit it.
- Headers set on main routes but missing on static files.
Verify:
- [ ] One helper covers all replies.
- [ ] 404 replies carry the headers.
- [ ] No X-Powered-By.
- [ ] The header test passes.
Output: security-headers.mjs, wiring in server.mjs, test/headers.test.mjs.

examples.input: quais headers de seguranca meu servidor node deve mandar
examples.output: applySecurityHeaders for every reply, HSTS only on HTTPS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, header test
